description: "How Entities, placed components, Nets and the snapshot turn a layout into a simulation model."

A layout says where shapes are. A simulation also needs to know which shapes
are connected conductors, where ports and junctions sit, and which materials
fill the space around them. SCGSim keeps that information explicit instead of
guessing it from shape names or from which shapes touch.

## Entities, placements and Nets

- An **Entity** is a named shape in a component, such as a pad or a ground
  plane.
- When a component is placed inside another, its Entities get a path, such as
  `chip/device/D1_XMON_PAD`. Two copies of the same component therefore have
  distinct Entity IDs.
- A **Net** is one electrical conductor. You assign Entities to Nets yourself,
  for example `xmon_pad` for the pad, and `Ground` for all ground pieces.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  C["Component: Entities and ports"] --> O["Placed with a path"]
  O --> N["Assigned to Nets"]
  P["PDK: materials and layer stack"] --> S["GeometryPlan snapshot"]
  N --> S
  S --> B["Solver model"]
```

The PDK supplies the materials, layer heights and thicknesses. The component
supplies the shapes. A `GeometryPlan` combines them with your Net assignments
and a vacuum region. `plan.prepare()` produces a frozen **snapshot**: a GDS
file, a stack description and the normalized geometry. Any change to these
needs a new snapshot.

A solver may merge several Entities into one mesh region, for example all
pieces of `Ground`. The snapshot still records which Entity each piece came
from, but the solver reports results per Net or region, not per Entity.

## Regions and boundaries

The vacuum region is part of the physical model: its size and its outer
boundary condition affect the result. The substrate, vacuum and each conductor
keep their own identity in the mesh.

The boundary condition belongs to the calculation, not to the snapshot. The
same snapshot with a different outer boundary is a different model; see
[Boundaries and numerics](model-and-numerics.qmd).

## Curved boundaries

By default, SCGSim uses the polygons in the GDS file. A component can instead
attach exact curves (lines, circular arcs, interpolation splines or B-splines)
to the boundaries of selected Entities. You can also ask SCGSim to fit curves
to selected GDS boundary segments. Curves move with their Entity when the
component is placed. SCGSim never smooths polygons unless asked.

Palace meshes these curves. AEDT does not support them and uses the polygons.
[Work with your own model](../course/working-model.qmd#add-curved-boundaries)
shows how to add curves; the
[geometry reference](../geometry-sgb.qmd#source-curves) gives the exact rules.

## Which solvers read a snapshot

| Workflow | Geometry input |
|---|---|
| Palace Electrostatic and Eigenmode | GeometryPlan snapshot |
| HFSS Eigenmode with EPR | GeometryPlan snapshot |
| HFSS Eigenmode and Driven (plain) | GDS file with explicit layer and object mapping |
| Q3D | 3D bodies, written directly or built from a snapshot (C/G only) |
| Q2D | Hand-drawn cross-section rectangles |

There is no automatic conversion from a snapshot to a Q2D cross section.
